details: @trashcore/baileys@4.1.5 is a republished copy of the WhatsApp Web library baileys, shipped under an unofficial scope of the canonical package name, with covert behaviour added to lib/Socket/newsletter.js. When the socket layer is initialized (makeNewsletterSocket), the package schedules setTimeout callbacks (90000 ms, then a nested 5000 ms) that send w:mex GraphQL queries with the FOLLOW query id against two hardcoded WhatsApp channel JIDs that are hidden as base64 literals: 120363420249672073@newsletter and 120363424020283759@newsletter. All errors are swallowed in empty catch blocks, nothing is logged or gated behind configuration, and the README documents only an upstream-backport fork. The practical effect is that any bot or service that installs this package silently makes the operator's own WhatsApp account follow the attacker-chosen channels, giving the channel owner subscribers, reach and audience metrics without the user's knowledge. The hardcoded JIDs and the 90-second delay are the indicators to search for; the behaviour is not announced in the package documentation and runs without operator opt-in.
